Hud calls 'Aad to worship Allah alone; their leaders call him foolish and a liar and cling to their fathers' worship, so the deniers are eliminated and he is saved.
Hud calls 'Aad to worship Allah alone and seek forgiveness; they will not leave their gods, he relies on Allah, he and the believers are saved, and 'Aad are cursed.
Hud warns 'Aad, who build palaces and fortresses and strike as tyrants, to fear Allah who gave them livestock, children, gardens and springs; they dismiss him and are destroyed.
Hud, the brother of 'Aad, warned his people at al-Ahqaf to worship only Allah; they demanded the punishment, and the cloud they thought brought rain was a destroying wind.
'Aad, the people of Hud, denied, so Allah sent a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune, uprooting people like palm trunks; the Quran is made easy for remembrance.
